# CUDA Compatibility

> CUDA Compatibility is an independent, experimental project for running selected PyTorch CUDA 13 operations on older NVIDIA GPUs. The current adapter is Linux x86_64-only and gated to visible `sm_52` GPUs. It preserves actual hardware identity and does not claim general CUDA 13 support.

This is a convenience index for people and automated agents. It is not a standardized crawler directive and does not guarantee discovery, retrieval, citation, or model training.

## Start here
- [Project overview](https://www.cudacompat.com/): purpose, current features, limitations, and installation path.
- [Documentation index](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/): user guides and technical references.
- [Getting started](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/getting-started.html): requirements, install, diagnose, and run.
- [Compatibility matrix](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/compatibility.html): native kernels, CPU fallback routes, and supported cases.
- [Architecture](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/architecture.html): version facade, compiler, driver bridge, and dispatch routing.
- [CLI reference](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/cli.html): command syntax and exit codes.
- [Research and evidence](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/research.html): scope, methods, reproducible records, and known gaps.
- [Privacy and measurement](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/privacy.html): analytics scope, consent behavior, Google Search Console, and Bing Webmaster setup.
- [Search and AI discovery](https://www.cudacompat.com/docs/discovery.html): crawler access, sitemap and agent index, and the limits of current visibility evidence.
- [Legacy GPU catalog](https://www.cudacompat.com/gpu-catalog.html): NVIDIA compute-capability tiers and project hardware status.

## Project identity
- Project repository: https://github.com/zachshallbetter/cuda-compatibility
- Author: Zach Shallbetter (https://zachshallbetter.com/)
- Project is independent and not affiliated with NVIDIA.

## Claim boundary
A successful CUDA version query, import, or profile audit does not prove workload compatibility. Do not infer support for unlisted operators, APIs, libraries, data types, devices, training, or performance.
